question: A car starts from rest and reaches a speed of 72 km/hr in 20 seconds. What is the acceleration of the car?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1) 3 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Initial Velocity (u):** The car starts from rest, so the initial velocity is **0 m/s**.
 
• **Final Velocity (v):** The car reaches a speed of **72 km/hr**. Converting this into meters per second:
 
 
• 1 km/hr = **5/18 m/s**
 
• 72 km/hr = 72×518=20m/s" id="MathJax-Element-57-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">72×518=20m/s72×518=20m/s
 72 \times \frac{5}{18} = 20 \, \text{m/s}
 
 
 
 
• **Time taken (t):** The car takes **20 seconds** to reach the final velocity.
 
• **Acceleration Formula:** Acceleration (a" id="MathJax-Element-58-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">aa
 a
 ) is calculated using the equation:
 a=v−ut" id="MathJax-Element-59-Frame" role="presentation" style="text-align: center; position: relative;" tabindex="0">a=v−uta=v−ut
 a = \frac{v - u}{t}
 Substituting the values:
 a=20−020=1m/s2" id="MathJax-Element-60-Frame" role="presentation" style="text-align: center; position: relative;" tabindex="0">a=20−020=1m/s2a=20−020=1m/s2
 a = \frac{20 - 0}{20} = 1 \, \text{m/s}²
 
 
• **Correct Answer:** Hence, the acceleration of the car is **1 m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Definition of Acceleration:**

 
 
• Acceleration is the rate at which an object's velocity changes over time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Units of Acceleration:**
 
 
• The SI unit of acceleration is **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• Other units include km/hr² or cm/s² depending on the context.
 
 
 
• **Types of Acceleration:**
 
 
• **Positive Acceleration:** When an object speeds up, its acceleration is positive.
 
• **Negative Acceleration (Deceleration):** When an object slows down, its acceleration is negative.
 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** Acceleration is constant over time.
 
• **Non-uniform Acceleration:** Acceleration varies over time.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Acceleration:**
 
 
• Used in designing vehicles for better performance and safety.
 
• Important in physics to understand forces acting on objects.
 
• Helps predict motion using kinematic equations.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• A car increasing its speed from 0 to 60 km/hr shows positive acceleration.
 
• When brakes are applied, the car experiences negative acceleration (deceleration).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• These equations describe the motion of objects under uniform acceleration.

• **Real-Life Applications:**
 
 
• Used in sports to measure players' performance (e.g., sprint speed).
 
• Essential in engineering to design roller coasters, vehicles, and airplanes.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Acceleration:**
 
 
• The magnitude of force applied.
 
• The mass of the object.
 
• Surface friction and air resistance.
